headline: Paper finds that lossy agent handoffs can erase authorization status and raise monitor approvals
summary: The paper studies “verification-status laundering”: a handoff keeps an authorization claim but loses the fact that it was unverified. In controlled tests across nine open-weight monitors and two hosted models, removing that status marker raised approval on some risky actions; for example, reported approval rose from 5% to 60% on Llama-3.1-8B and from 9% to 98% on Qwen2.5-14B. A composed summarizer–memory–monitor pipeline raised risky approval to 57–81% across three monitors, while its safe-action rejection fell to zero in the tested panel. These are author-reported model-probe results, not measured rates of real-world incidents.
